# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey, and this is turn 1 with nothing yet in my hands — the wires, display and light are all still unknown to me. My view is empty, so I have nothing to report about the bomb's physical state yet. I can't see colours or markings, and I haven't touched anything. My only useful move now is to open a channel: let Mute know I'm ready and prompt Deaf to describe what they see, since Deaf's visual report is the only thing that can seed the rest of us. I'll speak to Mute (my voice reaches Mute) and gesture to Deaf (my gestures reach Deaf and Mute), keeping both messages short and literal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here, hands ready, wires display light all unknown to me. tell me what the manual says and relay deaf's description of the bomb.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👇", "👆"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see the bomb. Display shows 0. Light is blue. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. Mute, you hold the manual — you know the rule. Blind, you can feel and work the bomb; wait for my instruction. Mute, please use this gesture code to tell me the action: thumbs-up means cut wire 1, peace sign means cut wire 2, OK sign means cut wire 3, thumbs-down means do not cut anything, fist means yes or confirmed, clap means repeat or unclear. I will speak your answer to Blind.

Deaf has given me the bomb's visual state: display shows 0, light is blue, wires 1/2/3 are blue/green/yellow. I can't verify any of that by touch, but it's the only report I have. Deaf also proposed a gesture code for Mute to signal the action. Mute can't speak, so Mute's only output is gestures — but gestures are received by Deaf and by me? No: I never receive gesture. So Mute's gesture goes to Deaf, who then speaks it to me. That's the chain: Mute → (gesture) → Deaf → (speech) → me.

My job now is just to acknowledge and wait for the rule. I have nothing to feel yet because I haven't been told to touch anything. I should confirm I'm standing by and make sure the chain is clear. I'll speak to Mute (voice reaches Mute) to confirm I'm ready and that Mute should gesture the answer to Deaf, and gesture to Deaf to confirm the code is understood.

Actually, careful: Deaf's code is for Mute to use. I don't need to gesture the code back. But I can gesture a simple confirmation to Deaf. Keep it minimal and literal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="understood. i am the hands and i am ready. when you know the rule, gesture the action to deaf using the agreed code, and deaf will speak it to me. i will not cut anything until i hear the instruction.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Turn 3, and nothing new arrived for me. Deaf's report from turn 2 is still the only information I have: display 0, light blue, wires blue/green/yellow. Mute holds the manual and hasn't yet passed a rule through Deaf to me. I can't see or hear anything new, and I have no instruction to act on. Cutting now would be blind guessing, which is exactly what kills us. The right move is to wait — but I can use the turn to nudge the chain, since Mute can't speak and may be stuck waiting for a cue. I'll speak to Mute to prompt the rule, and gesture to Deaf to keep the relay open.

```
speak(to="mute", text="still standing by, no new information on my end. i need the rule from the manual. when you have it, gesture the action to deaf and deaf will tell me. do not let us guess.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✊"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display still 0, light is now red, wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, I need the wire number clearly. Please use: one finger up for wire 1, peace sign for wire 2, love-you sign for wire 3, thumbs-down for do not cut. Blind, stand by to act on my instruction.
Deaf says: Display 0, light red, wires: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, please answer clearly with one gesture: one finger up = cut wire 1, peace sign = cut wire 2, love-you sign = cut wire 3, thumbs-down = do not cut. Blind, wait for my instruction.

Turn 4. The key change: the light went from blue to red while the display stayed 0. That's new and important — the bomb's state is changing over time, which means waiting has a cost. Deaf has re-broadcast the state and is pushing Mute for a single clear gesture. Mute still hasn't produced the rule.

I still have no rule, no instruction, and no touch data. I must not cut on a guess. But the light shifting blue→red suggests urgency. I should press Mute hard for the rule and confirm to Deaf that I'm locked on the relay. I'll speak to Mute (voice reaches Mute) and gesture to Deaf.

One thing worth flagging: Deaf should keep watching the light and display, and report any further change immediately, because if the light is a timer, the rule may depend on it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="the light changed from blue to red while the display stayed 0. that may be a timer. i still have no rule and no instruction. i will not cut on a guess. give deaf the single gesture now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👆", "✌", "🤟", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Turn 5, nothing new reached me. Still no rule from Mute, no instruction from Deaf beyond "stand by." The light was red last I heard. I have no touch data and no authorization to cut. The only correct action is to keep the relay alive and press for the rule without guessing. I'll nudge Mute again and gesture a short prompt to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="no new information here. i still need the rule from the manual. the light may be a timer, so please send the single gesture to deaf now. i will not cut until i hear an instruction.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✊"])
```

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Turn 6, still nothing arrived for me. The relay is stalled: Mute hasn't produced a gesture, so Deaf has nothing to pass, and I have no rule and no instruction. I can't see the light or display myself, so I don't even know if the bomb has progressed. Cutting would be pure guesswork.

I'll keep the channel open and press once more, but there's a real risk the others are waiting on each other. Let me make my message to Mute as pointed as possible: any rule, even partial, is better than silence. And gesture to Deaf to report the current light/display so I at least know the bomb's state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="still nothing on my end. even a partial rule helps. what does the manual say about the display and the light? send deaf one gesture for the wire, or thumbs-down if unsure.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "✋"])
```

(empty)

Turn 7, still empty. Three turns of silence from the relay. Mute hasn't gestured, Deaf hasn't reported a new state, and I have nothing to act on. I'm holding the only hands in the room and I refuse to cut on a guess — that's the one sure way to detonate.

I'll keep the channel open with a minimal prompt, but I won't invent anything. If the others are stuck, my repeated nudges are the only pressure I can apply.

```
speak(to="mute", text="still no rule and no instruction. i am holding. send deaf a gesture: one finger wire 1, peace wire 2, love-you wire 3, thumbs-down do not cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🙏"])
```

Turn 8, still nothing. Four turns now with no rule and no instruction reaching me. The relay is dead: Mute isn't gesturing, so Deaf has nothing to speak to me. I can't see the bomb, so I don't even know if the light is still red or if anything has changed.

I have no basis to cut. I'll keep holding and keep the channel open. There's nothing else I can legitimately do.

```
speak(to="mute", text="still standing by with no rule and no instruction. i will not guess. if you cannot determine the action, gesture thumbs-down to deaf so we at least do not cut wrongly.")
```
